3. Where there are several issues, the burden of proving some of which lies on the other party, the party beginning may, at his option, either produce his evidence on those issues or reserve it by way of answer to the evidence produced by the other party; and in the latter case, the party beginning may produce evidence on those issues after the other party has produced all his evidence, and the other may then reply, specially on the evidence so produced by the party beginning; but the party beginning will then be entitled to reply generally on the whole." 

 Section 138 of the Evidence Act has provided the order of examination of the witnesses and along with the above provisions of law if the concept of burden of proof as spelt out in sections 101, 102 and 103 of the said Act are considered in a cohesive manner it would be manifest that mere stating or alleging facts in the pleading are not enough to establish a legal right, be it preemption under the Mohammedan Law or any other suits/proceedings under any other law. It also does not require any elaboration by writing so many pages that the plaintiffs have to succeed on their own legs and cannot succeed on the weakness of the defendant's case, if any. In view of the specific pleading of the plaintiffs, plaintiff No. 1 performed the legal formalities of talab-e-mowasibat and talab-e-Ishaad which are essentially questions of fact onus was upon them to prove those. Keeping in view the provisions of law and the settled legal principle as indicated hereinbefore let us see how far the plaintiffs proved the facts as asserted in paragraph 4 of the plaint.
